text.p: Moldova's parliament on Friday narrowly passed the 1997 budget after almost six months of protracted debate.

"This budget...will assure the payment of urgent needs such as wages and pensions, but it also demands tough financial discipline," Finance Minister Valeriu Chitan told reporters after the draft was approved by 54 votes, just one above the needed simple majority.
The draft provides for a 330 milion lei ($71 million) deficit, three percent of the gross domestic product with revenues of 1,916.5 million lei and expenditures of 2,246.5 million lei.
Work on the budget, which by law should be approved by December 15 of the previous year, had been delayed by December presidential elections and forming of a new government.

Chitan said his ministry's top priority was to boost tax collection. At present only 65 percent of taxes are collected, and the government seeks to raise the figure to 80-85 percent by the end of the year.

The government plans to raise 195 million lei from issuing government securities to partly cover the budget deficit. National Bank credits to the government worth 50 million, and foreign loans are expected to raise another 85 million lei.
According to the Finance Ministry's preliminary data, the 1996 budget deficit was 474 million lei, or 5.3 percent of gross domestic product. $1 = 4,65 lei
